[{"heading": "Antetokounmpo heroic as Bucks beat Suns to capture 1st title since 1971 / Milwaukee superstar named Finals MVP after 50-point, 14 rebound performance", "text": "Giannis Antetokounmpo had the Larry O'Brien Trophy in one arm, the NBA Finals MVP trophy in the other and there was a cigar on the table in front of him.

All the work it took to lift the Milwaukee Bucks from a team that won 15 games when he was a rookie to one with 16 wins this postseason was finally finished.

"This is time to celebrate," Antetokounmpo said.

Milwaukee waited 50 years for that.

Antetokounmpo ended one of the greatest NBA Finals ever with 50 points, 14 rebounds and five blocked shots as the Bucks beat the Phoenix Suns 105-98 on Tuesday night to win an entertaining series 4-2 and cap off a joyous return to a fan-filled postseason after last year's NBA bubble."}, {"heading": "Antetokounmpo heroic as Bucks beat Suns to capture 1st title since 1971 / Milwaukee superstar named Finals MVP after 50-point, 14 rebound performance", "text": "It was the third game this series with at least 40 points and 10 rebounds for Antetokounmpo, a dominant debut finals performance that takes its place among some of the game's greatest. Antetokounmpo finished with 35.2 points, 13.2 rebounds and 5.0 assists per game while shooting 61.8%, the first player in finals history to reach those numbers.

He shot 16 for 25 from the field and made an unbelievable 17-of-19 free throws — a spectacular showing for any shooter, let alone one who was hitting just 55.6% in the postseason and was ridiculed for it at times.

"People told me I can't make free throws and I made them tonight. And I'm a freaking champion," Antetokounmpo said."}, {"heading": "Antetokounmpo heroic as Bucks beat Suns to capture 1st title since 1971 / Milwaukee superstar named Finals MVP after 50-point, 14 rebound performance", "text": "He hopped around the court waving his arms with 20 seconds remaining to encourage fans to cheer, but there was no need. Their voices had been booming inside and outside for hours by then, having waited 50 years to celebrate a winner after Lew Alcindor — before becoming Kareem Abdul-Jabbar — and Oscar Robertson led the Bucks to their first championship in 1971.

BOX SCORE: Bucks 105, Suns 98

Bucks defeat Suns, move 1 win away from 1st NBA title since 1971

In a season played played largely without fans, the Bucks had 65,000 of them packed into the Deer District outside, a wild party that figured to last deep into the Midwestern night. The party wasn't bad inside, either: Confetti rained down inside as fans chanted "Bucks in 6! Bucks in 6!" — a hopeful boast by former player that turned out to be a prophetic rallying cry.

"I hope they enjoyed it just like we are now," Middleton added."}]

[{"heading": "Milwaukee Bucks defeat Phoenix Suns to win the NBA championship, led by star forward Giannis Antetokounmpo", "text": "The Milwaukee Bucks have won their first NBA championship since 1971, downing the Phoenix Suns in game 6 of the NBA finals.

Playing on their home court in Milwaukee, the Bucks beat the Suns 105-98 to win in six games, after losing the opening two contests of the series.

Explain what Tailscale Serve does.

Tailscale Serve allows a user to expose a local service running on a specific port within their Tailscale tailnet. When a local port is served, the service becomes accessible via a unique URL within the tailnet, such as `https://vps.tail1234.ts.net`, which proxies traffic to the local service (e.g., `http://127.0.0.1:3000`).

The `--bg` flag runs the serve command in the background, storing the configuration persistently so it survives shell closure, reboots, and `tailscale down` followed by `tailscale up`. The command to disable a background serve handler is `tailscale serve --https=443 off`, and it must use the same flags that were used to create the handler.

Tailscale Serve supports path-based routing, allowing multiple local services to be served under different paths on the same hostname. For example, one service can be mounted at the root (`/`), another at `/api`, and a third at `/grafana`, with the longest matching path determining which service handles a request.

The `--set-path` flag specifies the path for a service mount, and it accepts the path with or without a leading slash; the CLI automatically adds the slash if missing. The current configuration can be checked using `sudo tailscale serve status`, which lists the hostname and each mounted path.

The underlying implementation verifies the node has the necessary capabilities (e.g., funnel) and checks for conflicts, such as using the `--service` flag only in background mode or not supporting `--service` with `funnel`. The serve configuration is managed via the node's persistent configuration and stored in the local preferences, with validation and conflict handling in place.

[{"heading": "HTTP 204 No Content: Meaning, Use Cases, and Best Practices / What is HTTP 204 No Content?", "text": "The 204 No Content is an HTTP status code that indicates a request succeeded, but the server intentionally returns no message body. The server has successfully processed the requested resource and isn’t returning any content because there’s nothing meaningful to send back.

Think of it like a CI run that ends with “Build succeeded.” The job’s done, everything passed, and there’s nothing more to report.

Unlike redirect codes (301, 302) that send the client to a new URL, 204 is a terminal response that requires no further action. The HTTP response completes immediately without any HTML content or data payload.

**A 204 tells the client:**

- Your request was successful.
- The operation completed as expected.

introduced the `fold` attribute on datetime objects to
